question.leadin: The final holder of this title was Tokugawa Yoshinobu.
question.text: Prior to an 1868 restoration of imperial rule, what title was held by military rulers of Japan?
question.clue: A power vacuum created after the death of a holder of this title led to the Onin War, which initiated the Sengoku period.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about emperors of Japan.
swap.text: This man has the distinction of maintaining the longest reign of any Japanese emperor. He is more famously known for overseeing the Japanese surrender during World War II.
swap.clue: This ruler, who delivered the Jewel Voice Broadcast, later renounced his divinity in the Humanity Declaration.

question.leadin: Give the following about surprise attacks in Japanese history.
question.text: In the 1560 Battle of Okehazama, this daimyo's forces sneaked to the rear of the opposing army, killing the opposing leader at his tent. This unifier of Japan was succeeded by Toyotomi Hideyoshi and Tokugawa Ieyasu.
question.clue: This man's troops used matchlocks to repulse the charge of Takeda cavalry at the Battle of Nagashino.

swap.text: Prior to the Perry Expedition, the only Japanese port that was largely open to foreigners was this city on the southern island of Kyushu. It later became the second city to be hit with an atomic bomb during World War II.
swap.clue: Trade between this city and Macau was carried out by non-American "black ships."

question.leadin: Rudolf von Gneist helped create a new constitution during this period.
question.text: Name this period in Japanese history following the end of the Tokugawa Shogunate. This period is named for an emperor whose reign saw a resurgence of imperial power.
question.clue: This period saw a diplomatic mission proposed by Guido Verbeck called the Iwakura mission.

swap.text: This was the first city ever to be hit by a nuclear bomb. The B-29 Enola Gay was responsible for the dropping of the uranium "Little Boy" bomb on this Japanese city.
swap.clue: A bell with the phrase "know yourself" commemorates an incident in this city that created the first hibakusha ("HEE-ba-KOO-sha").

question.leadin: Answer the following about Japanese history prior to the Meiji Restoration.
question.text: This city was the capital of Japan until Emperor Meiji made Tokyo the capital in 1868.
question.clue: Companies with headquarters in this city include Nichicon, Murata, and Ninetendo.

swap.leadin: During this period, emperors who retired to monasteries retained power in the system of cloistered rule.
swap.text: Name this period that succeeded the Nara Period. This period came to an end with the Genpei War.
swap.clue: Go-Sanjo and Shirawaka established the "cloistered emperor" or "insei" system during this period, which was dominated by the Fujiwara clan.

question.leadin: Of the hundreds of exploding balloons sent by this group to the U.S., only one managed to cause any damage, landing in Oregon and killing several schoolchildren who checked it out.
question.text: Name this group within the Epidemic Prevention and Purification Department. A guy actually named Colonel Sanders brought it to the attention of Douglas MacArthur, who pardoned its leader in exchange for scientific data.
question.answerHtml: Unit 731 [or Nana-san-ichi Butai, or Manchu Detachment 731, or 731 Regiment, or Ishii Unit]
question.clue: This research group under the Kwantung Army committed some of the greatest Japanese crimes against humanity during the war. It was commanded by Shiro Ishii, who was pardoned by the United States after the war in exchange for his data.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about the Tokugawa shogunate.
swap.text: In 1638, the Tokugawa government put down this rebellion of Japanese Christians by storming Hara Castle and beheading its leader, Shiro.
swap.clue: The Tokugawa Shogunate put down this 1630s rebellion of Japanese Catholics that led to the expulsion of Portuguese traders.

question.leadin: Identify the following about a nation's history.
question.text: During the Muromachi period this clan held the shogunate. Members included Takauji and Yoshimitsu.
question.clue: A ruler of this family promoted the "Higashiyama culture" of the eastern hills, which popularized shoin ("sho-een") homes with tatami floors; his aesthetic was exemplified by the "wabi-sabi" style of a temple that he couldn't afford to coat in silver.

swap.leadin: To show repentance, some members of this organization will cut off their fingers which makes them easily identifiable for police.
swap.text: Identify this international organized crime syndicate primarily based in Japan.
swap.answerHtml: yakuza [accept bōryokudan or gokudō or ninkyō dantai which ironically means "chivalrous organization"]
swap.clue: They often have full back tattoos and fashion themselves as "town-defenders," or machi-yokko.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the geography of Japan.
question.text: This island chain off the southern tip of Kyushu, which includes Okinawa, was annexed during the Meiji period. Its natives speak an eponymous language which is the only surviving sister of Japanese.
question.clue: Tei Do, a commander for this kingdom, was executed after failing to surrender to invading Satsuma forces.

swap.leadin: Name these dudes from Asian history who founded dynasties.
swap.text: After the Taira clan was defeated in the Battle of Dannoura, ending the Genpei War, this man became the first shogun of the Kamakura dynasty.
swap.clue: This man seduced the daughter of his warden after he was banished to Izu for twenty years when his father tried to remove Taira Kiyomori in the Heiji Disturbance.

question.text: This period, in which Suiko ("soo-ee-ko") and Shotoku ruled, saw several notable Korean monks such as Illa and Hyepyeon ("h'YEH-pyun") establish themselves in Japan. This period lies between the Kofun and Nara periods.
question.clue: Prince Shotoku proclaimed the Confucian 17 Article Constitution during this period, part of a series of moves to adopt Chinese customs.

swap.leadin: The massive temple complex of Todai-ji was constructed during this period as the center of a system of provincial temples known as kokubun-ji.
swap.text: Name this period of Japanese history in the 8th century that began with the establishment of Heijo-kyo as the capital. This period was followed by the Heian ("HAY-on") period.
swap.clue: This was the first time when emperors adopted the title of "tenno," and other innovations during this period, such as the institution of a Council of State, were adopted in order to imitate the government at Changan and important Tang Chinese institutions.

question.text: With the Asuka Period, the Kofun Period forms part of this period of Japanese history when the imperial capital was at Nara. This period shares its name with Japan's primary ethnic group and with the Japanese battleship that was the country's flagship for most of World War Two.

swap.text: In the 18th and 19th centuries, this name was given to the study of Western science and medicine from translated books obtained through trade on Dejima Island.
swap.clue: This process, which was made possible by the allowance of traders on the island of Dejima, allowed its country to understand contemporary scientific progress despite its sakoku isolationist policies.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Empress Saimi, who reigned from 642 to 645 AD if we are to believe the historical record.
question.text: That data appears in this chronicle, which like the Kojiki, is semi-mythical. The first petrochemical oil spill in ancient literature appears in this text's chronicle of Emperor Tenji.
question.clue: This set of chronicles, the most comprehensive text available for scholarship on Ancient Japan. It was completed under the supervision of Prince Toneri and presented to Empress Gensho in the year 720.

swap.text: The foremost predecessor of the LDP was the Liberal Party, which was led by this towering figure of post-WWII Japanese politics. He served as Prime Minister five times between 1946 and 1954, and formulated a namesake Doctrine for Japan's postwar recovery.
